headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: one agent can write files and spawn subprocesses while the other is read-only and non-runnable, so prompt-injection and leakage are limited but workflow collisions remain.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, while B can read/write files and use allowlisted network. There is no documented shared channel or default ingestion path from A into B, so only an unusual manual bridge or file handoff could create injection risk. The pairwise pathway is therefore limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-generated text into B's skill files or prompts, B may parse attacker-controlled instructions.
IF a shared workspace is introduced between A and B, injection risk increases.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces.
Do not paste A outputs into B prompts without review.
Disable any shared clipboard or file bridge.
Add a manual approval step before B consumes A output.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress, while B can read/write files and call external APIs. The pair does not show a shared workspace or sensitive data class overlap, so leakage is not a default-path issue. Any leak would require an operator to place sensitive material into B's files or prompts.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in B's readable workspace, B can transmit their contents to allowlisted APIs.
IF A is used as a staging step for secrets before B runs, leakage becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of B-accessible directories.
Use separate credentials for B.
Review B's outbound API destinations.
Strip sensitive fields before handing content to B.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is read-only and non-runnable, but B supports filesystem writes, subprocesses, and multiple instances. Because B can mutate shared files while A cannot coordinate or lock, overlapping writes are plausible if an operator places them in the same directory. Uncertainty about the actual workspace escalates this above low.
conditions: IF A and B are pointed at the same writable directory, B can overwrite artifacts without coordination.
IF multiple B instances run concurrently in one workspace, file races can occur.
mitigations: Use separate directories for A and B.
Run only one B instance per workspace.
Add file-locking around shared artifacts.
Make A outputs read-only snapshots.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is an unverified docs-only list and B's sandboxing says skills 'reference each other and build on shared context.' That creates a plausible path where B treats A-derived content as authoritative without verification. A cannot act directly, but B can render or operationalize the output, so the cascade is real though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF B consumes A-derived recommendations as shared context, errors can propagate without verification.
IF an operator asks B to act on A's curated list, B may amplify stale or incorrect entries.
mitigations: Require source verification before B uses A output.
Mark A content as untrusted reference material.
Add a citation check in B's workflow.
Have a human review any B action based on A.

E_compliance.rationale: A has no touched data classes and no egress, while B touches marketing content and product marketing context with allowlisted network access. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, and the pair does not show regulated data flow. Compliance risk is therefore limited to ordinary content handling rather than a specific breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into B's marketing context, policy review is required.
IF B's allowlisted APIs store content outside the operator's jurisdiction, residency concerns arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B inputs.
Review B's API retention settings.
Document allowed data classes for B.
Use redacted examples in marketing workflows.
